title: ICP strategy & segment priorities
summary: Conduit’s published ICP is hospitality stay operators—hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers—not a job-title list. Named proof is strongest for vacation-rental managers, thinner for independent hotels, and still a marketing claim for hotel groups; unit, employee, and revenue cutoffs are not fit gates.
markdown:
Conduit’s public ICP is a hospitality **account**, not a jobs list. The pricing FAQ says Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, with AI agents that answer guest messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate work with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Global navigation names three industries in this order: short-term rentals, independent hotels, hotel groups. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Fit** means the company operates guest stays, can supply property-specific policies and reservation context, and runs conversations on channels Conduit unifies, with humans for handoffs. A motivated buyer outside that operating model does not create fit. Investigation priority follows evidence strength in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence), not invented market size: named stories cluster in vacation-rental / property-management companies; independent hotels have one boutique P&L write-up plus an industry page; hotel groups have product copy without a named group case body in this pack; serviced apartments are named in the FAQ only.

## Who is a good-fit account

A good-fit account is an operator of stays whose guest work is communication-heavy and **property-specific**. Agents use the operator’s property information and policies, act through supported connected tools, and follow rules for what the team should handle. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Inbox assumes conversations can be organized by property or team, with stay and booking context from connected PMS and OTA accounts beside the thread. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

Hotels and vacation-rental operators are both in-category and **not the same test**. Independent-hotel pages stress after-hours calls, front-desk load, Opera / Mews / Cloudbeds, and extras such as room upgrades, spa, and dining. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels) Short-term rental pages stress per-listing knowledge, Airbnb / Vrbo / Booking.com / Expedia threads, check-in instructions, and booking-change requests. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals) Hotel-group pages add shared brand standards with per-property policies and reservation details. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups) Run [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels) and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals) as separate account tests. Serviced-apartment operators belong in the same FAQ sentence; investigate them as in-category until disproven—do not reject for a missing named story.

Company reach copy (“300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries”) is a Conduit claim, not named-account proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

## Priority buying situations

These are situations that appear in named stories or industry pages. They are research prompts, not needs every customer has.

| Situation observed | Where it shows up | Why it is investigable | Evidence strength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guest volume growing faster than support headcount | STR / PM companies | Haven and HomeHop describe scale without proportional guest-support hiring; Canbnb separately describes message volume and AI handling, not a proven flat-headcount result | Strong named STR stories |
| Overnight / after-hours coverage | Hotels and STR | Independent-hotel after-hours receptionist; HomeHop voice coverage 1–7 AM | Industry page + named STR story |
| Split inboxes or generic helpdesk misfit | Luxury PM | Bocobay left Intercom to unify WhatsApp, email, phone, and live chat | One named migration |
| Acquisition or multi-market expansion without a new comms team | STR / multi-country | Cascadia’s first PM acquisition; Cosmica Italy/Dubai; Wynwood seven countries | Strong STR / CX stories |
| Owner wants leaner or more passive operations | Boutique hotel | Lauderdale replaced a call-center model and reports support-cost and NOI changes | One hotel story |

Do not treat 90% automation, modeled asset value, or any single automation rate as a qualification bar. Those figures stay attributed in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Company characteristics

No public source sets employee, revenue, or unit-count **fit gates**. Pricing publishes commercial bands only: Startup for 0–25 units, per-unit packages “from independent teams to enterprise,” and starting rates that scale beyond 50 listings. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) A small portfolio can be commercially eligible; a ~270-property manager can be a named customer. Neither is a necessary ICP cutoff.

| Characteristic | What sources show | Fit implication | Still unknown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Industry | Hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, STR managers | Primary in-category test | Resorts, villas, aparthotels appear as marketing links, not a defined ICP |
| Ownership vs management | Owner-operator hotel (Lauderdale); PM brands managing listings (Haven, Cascadia, HomeHop, Canbnb, Bocobay) | Contracting party may be owner or manager | Franchise vs brand vs asset manager not specified |
| Geography / language | Company claim of 120+ countries; named stories in the US, Australia, Italy, Dubai, Caribbean, Latin America/Europe, Bali, London/SF | Geography is not a published exclusion | Multilingual replies are marketed, but required-language quality and channel coverage must be confirmed for the actual workflow |
| Portfolio complexity | Inbox views by property or team; hotel-group shared KB; STR per-listing KB | Multi-property / multi-listing is how the product is demonstrated | No required property count |
| Systems | Hotel examples Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds; STR examples Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Airbnb | Check live connectors in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations) | A logo is not proof of a supported agent action |

## Buyer roles versus company fit

Company fit is the lodging model and guest-operations stack. Buyer roles are how that account buys and runs the product. Founders, CEOs, guest-services leads, and CX heads appear in stories; those titles are not the ICP. Map influence in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles). If the company does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental stays, a strong champion does not create fit. If the company is in-category, a missing named persona is a research gap, not a reject.

## Readiness and urgency

Readiness the sources actually describe: connected channels and PMS/OTA context; a knowledge base of property policies; escalation rules; people who review handoffs. Haven’s story says Conduit was already installed at about 40% automation with listings uploaded, no workflows, and minimal knowledge-base work until the team standardized answers. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) Docs-style product FAQ copy says how much agents resolve depends on guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md)

Urgency is not a published score. Named stories involve growth, staffing, acquisitions, overnight coverage, and owner valuation. Test whether those situations exist with [Qualification & account research playbook](#knowledge/buying-triggers). Do not invent a buying attitude or timeline. Package choice (Messaging vs Guest vs devices vs Full Suite) is commercial mapping in [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) after the account is in-category. Capabilities live in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities).

## Exclusions and unknowns

Sources do not publish a negative ICP. Do not reject for unknown unit count, missing hotel-group proof, or an integration that is only a logo—investigate.

The practical out-of-category signal is an account that does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays. That follows the FAQ; it is not a legal exclusion list. Hybrid real-estate-plus-hospitality operators that still run guest stays (Wynwood) remain in-category.

Material gaps: named proof for hotel groups and serviced apartments; whether “unit” equals listing, room, or key; franchise buying units; language product limits; whether Operations (nav: coming soon) is required for group ops use cases. Preserve the contradiction that Full Suite already lists workforce/operations lines while the product nav still says Operations is coming soon. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## What the company must confirm

Before treating segments as equally proven, confirm: hotel-group and serviced-apartment referenceability; billable unit vs listing vs room; which PMS/OTA paths actually write bookings, tasks, or payments for this stack; which required guest languages and channels are supported at the needed quality; and whether the contracting party is owner, management company, or brand. Until then, prioritize STR/PM investigation, keep independent hotels in-category with thinner proof, and treat hotel groups as marketed but under-evidenced.
open_questions: Is there named, body-complete proof for hotel groups comparable to STR stories?
Which serviced-apartment operators are referenceable, and how do they differ from hotels and STRs in buying unit?
Does Conduit bill a unit as a listing, room, key, or something else—and is that ever a fit rule or only packaging?
Who contracts—owner, management company, franchisee, or brand—and does that change qualification?
Which languages and locales are product-supported versus outcomes reported only in the Wynwood story?

icp_criteria.criterion: Account operates hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays
icp_criteria.rationale: The pricing FAQ names these three operator types as who Conduit is for.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm lodging model from the company site, OTA/PMS presence, and match to independent-hotel, hotel-group, or short-term rental industry pages.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If the noun is adjacent (resort, villa, aparthotel, hybrid real-estate hospitality), investigate against industry pages; do not reject solely because the FAQ used a different label.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest conversations can use a confirmed Conduit channel path
icp_criteria.rationale: A supported channel path enables the intended workflow; property/team views are product capabilities, not a minimum portfolio-size rule.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Identify actual guest channels and confirm their connection path. Single-property and multi-property operators can both qualify.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Research unknown channels. Do not reject a single-property operator or an account whose current inbox is not segmented.

icp_criteria.criterion: Vacation-rental or short-term rental management company
icp_criteria.rationale: Named customer stories with operating detail cluster in STR/PM companies; industry page exists for this segment.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm STR listings, channel mix, and management vs owner-operator model; use the vacation-rental ICP doc for the deeper test.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If hybrid hotel-plus-rental, score both hotel and rental tests separately.

icp_criteria.rationale: Independent hotels are a named industry; Lauderdale is the named hotel P&L story in this pack.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm hotel (not only STR) operations, front-desk/after-hours load, and hotel-oriented PMS names such as Opera, Mews, or Cloudbeds.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Thin named proof is a proof gap, not a reason to mark the account out-of-category.

icp_criteria.criterion: Hotel group with shared brand standards and per-property policies
icp_criteria.rationale: Hotel-group pages market multi-property brand standards, but this source pack has no named hotel-group case body.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm multiple hotels, shared vs local procedures, and group vs property buying unit.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Treat as marketed in-category; do not assume conversion or outcomes equal STR stories until references exist.

icp_criteria.criterion: Connected PMS or OTA that can supply reservation/listing context
icp_criteria.rationale: Agents and inbox claims depend on property information, reservation data, and connected tools; connector depth varies.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Name the PMS/OTA and check it against the integrations guide; confirm messaging vs reservation-data-only path.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Unknown stack is investigate, not reject. A logo is not evidence of write-back.

icp_criteria.criterion: Capacity to document property policies and set escalation rules
icp_criteria.rationale: Haven was installed at ~40% automation until knowledge-base and workflow work; agent resolution is described as depending on knowledge, integrations, and rules.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask whether listings/policies are documented, who owns the knowledge base, and what must stay human.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Low current documentation is a readiness gap, not automatic unfit.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest-support volume, after-hours coverage, or call-center cost creating a live operating pressure
icp_criteria.rationale: Named stories involve headcount, overnight coverage, acquisitions, and call-center replacement; none of these is stated as a required trigger.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask how nights, peaks, and current support vendors are staffed; record dates and vendors.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Missing urgency does not fail fit; log it for sequencing only.

icp_criteria.criterion: Business that does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays
icp_criteria.rationale: Published industries and the who-is-for FAQ are hospitality stay operators; no source targets other verticals.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: If the company has no guest-stay inventory or guest-communication operation, mark out-of-category.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Hybrids that still run guest stays remain in-category pending investigation.

evidence_validation: Exact passages checked; interpretation and proposed policies require review.

editorial_reviews.reason: Do not describe multilingual capability as absent when marketed explicitly; ask about workflow-specific coverage.
Resolve reviewed proof attribution, buying-role and connector readiness issues; preserve unknowns without manufacturing exclusions.
